items.title: Young Snooky — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: What was the name of that club? Ray Perry was playing, oh man, you making me think of some things that I.

ctx.x: And how long were you in Chick Carter‘s band?

I was with Chick Carter‘s band, well we did pretty good, the band got all the way to New York—then we played Apollo, I don‘t know—but the band got to New York and they got stranded. You know, back in them days, things happened to them. We stayed around that town for quite awhile before we could do anything, I don‘t think we played the Apollo. We thought we were going to play the Apollo but it didn‘t happen. We went on to Boston and played a club in Boston. What was the name of that club? Ray Perry was playing, oh…
We can come back to that, we can come back to that. So you played a club in Boston and then did you stay in Boston or did you then go back to New York or what?

items.title: Snooky Young and Gerald Wilson interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995
items.q: They had Ray Perry and Step Horton, and Snooky, and Eddie Byrd and all these great guys.

ctx.x: He makes no bones about it.

And at the moment it was great because it was a great thing to see this, because I would have loved to have played with that band. That was my favorite band. So, but I loved this little band of Chick Carter’s. And I says I’m not going to leave this band. So finally the day came a couple of nights later and we played this battle of the bands with Erskine Hawkins. And I knew Sammy Lowe and Dud Bascomb and Jimmy Mitchell and Avery Parrish. I knew all of these guys. Over the years I had met all of the bands that came…
Six months later, he had Lunceford send for me to join the band.
